:::{#thm-entropy-shift}
#### Shifting does not change entropy

Let $X$ be a [continuous random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-continuous-rv) with [entropy](#def-entropy) $\entropyf{X}$,
and let $c$ be a [real number](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/number-systems.html#def-real-numbers).
Then

$$\entropyf{X + c} = \entropyf{X}.$$

[@cover2006elements, Theorem 8.6.3]

:::

::: proof

Let $Y \eqdef X + c$.
The [density](random-variables.qmd#def-pdf) of $Y$ is

$$\p(Y=y) = \p(X=y-c).$$

At the value $y = x + c$, the density of $Y$ therefore matches the density of $X$ at $x$.
That relation holds at every value $x$,
so it holds between the [random variables](random-variables.qmd#def-random-variable).
So the [surprisal](#def-surprisal) of $X + c$ matches the surprisal of $X$:

$$\surprisalf{X + c} = \surprisalf{X}.$$

Hence

$$
\ba
\entropyf{X + c}
&= \E{\surprisalf{X + c}} && \text{(definition of entropy)} \\
&= \E{\surprisalf{X}} && \text{(surprisal of } X + c \text{)} \\
&= \entropyf{X}. && \text{(definition of entropy)}
\ea
$$

:::
